the X-ray absorption lines of NGC 3517 are due to a multi-component outflow, which has a velocity of about 1000-4000 km s{sup −1} and an ionization parameter of log (ξ) = 2–4.
the X-ray spectra from the 2001 and the 2006 observations of NGC 3515 are consistent with each other and with a simple picture of a single, broad, ionized outflow.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fast components appear only during the high state and not in the low state.
there is a fast, highly ionized, and highly variable component of the outflow, and a slower, lower ionization, and stable component that is present in the spectra of both epochs.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the X-ray spectra are dominated by the fast components, while the slow component has a negligible effect on the observed spectrum.
the fast outflowing gas has a higher ionization than previously thought, and that this gas is present only in the high X-ray flux state.
